title: Workflow Definition Descriptor
description: The meta-schema of the Workflow Definition Descriptor (WDD): the versioned, structured definition file the ballerina/workflow compiler plugin generates at build time and packs into the integration's executable JAR as the fixed-name resource 'workflow.def.json'. The descriptor captures only structural facts — what registers with the workflow runtime, plus JSON Schemas — never expression-valued instance parameters (roles, titles, retry counts, timeouts, payloads).

descriptorVersion.description: WDD spec version (major.minor). Minor versions are additive-only; consumers must not parse an unknown major.

package.description: The Ballerina package this descriptor describes.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of the document's canonical bytes (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) serialized without this field. Instance identity is (package.org, package.name, package.version, checksum).

workflows.description: Every @workflow:Workflow function in the package, sorted by name.

agents.description: Every module-level durable-agent declaration's static structure, sorted by name.

name.description: The registered workflow type (the function name, without the runtime's 'workflow-' prefix).

input.description: The workflow's start input as a single form: one property per data parameter. The slot's type is the parenthesized data-parameter list.
The activity's data parameters as a single form; also backs review 'proceed-with-input' forms.

output.description: The activity's return. The slot type records the full (possibly error-bearing) type; the schema describes the success members only.

name.description: The task name as written at the awaitHumanTask call site; qualified at runtime as <workflow>.<task>.

reviewActivities.description: Which activities are human-reviewed, and on which trigger. The review's proceed-with-input form is the activity's input slot — not repeated here.

graph.description: The workflow's execution graph. Null when the body performs no durable step.

name.description: The agent's stable identity: its module-level variable name.

tools.description: Declared capabilities advertised to the model. Runtime-added capabilities surface through runtime APIs only, never the descriptor.

graph.description: The agent's structure as a star graph.

functionRef.description: The implementation binding: the module-level function the runtime resolves and invokes for this structure. Structural — it is what registers with the runtime.

module.description: Qualified module name: <org>/<module> (the module name includes submodule parts, e.g. acme/procurement.ledger).

version.description: The module's major version — the granularity the runtime resolves symbols at.

typedSlot.description: A typed schema slot. The resolved Ballerina type descriptor is always recorded; the JSON Schema is a derived rendering emitted per representability tier: exact for closed anydata shapes, permissive + lossy for open anydata (json, anydata), omitted for the unrepresentable (xml, error, behavioral types, and composites mixing them into JSON data).

type.description: The resolved Ballerina type descriptor — the source of truth. For parameter-list inputs this is the parenthesized data-parameter list.

lossy.description: Present (true) when the schema is a permissive approximation of the type rather than an exact rendering — form generators should not over-promise validation.

schemaDocument.description: The pinned JSON Schema dialect: the exact 2020-12 subset the workflow runtime's TypesUtil emits. Extensions to this subset arrive only with WDD minor versions.

graph.description: The structure of one workflow or agent as a directed graph, for visualization and for joining an execution back to its source. A workflow's graph is its durable steps in source order, nested under the control flow that guards them; an agent's is a star, because the model — not the code — decides what runs when. A running execution reports the step it is at (`ActivityTreeNode.stepId`, `GraphNode.metadata.stepId`), so a viewer can highlight the path actually taken. Nodes without a `stepId` in the execution predate the runtime that stamps it, so consumers must treat the join as optional.

file.description: The source file the workflow's body was read from. Absent for an agent graph, which has no body.

nodes.description: The graph's nodes, in source order for a workflow.

stepId.description: Stable identity of this node within its workflow or agent. For a workflow: `<target>#<ordinal>` for a step, `<construct>#<ordinal>` for control flow (`if#1`, `while#2`, `match#1`, `do#1`, `wait#1`, `sleep#1`) — the ordinal counts occurrences in source order, so it survives reformatting and unrelated edits. For an agent: derived from the name (`agent`, `model`, `tool:<name>`, `event:<name>`, `task:<name>`).

kind.description: What the node is. Workflow graphs use the step and control-flow kinds; agent graphs use AGENT, MODEL, TOOL, HUMAN_TASK and EVENT. An EXIT is an early exit inside an arm — a return, fail or panic, named by `mode` — terminal (no outgoing edge) and never present in an execution, so a consumer may attribute a run to one only when it is the single exit consistent with the observed last step. A CODE node is a maximal run of consecutive non-durable statements, collapsed to one display-only node labelled by its statement count ('4 statements') so the diagram reads like the source; it carries no runtime meaning and never appears in an execution. A REVIEW is the human decision a gated step raises rather than a step control flows through: it hangs off the step by an edge labelled 'on failure' or 'before run', is never any step's predecessor, and on the happy path never happens — its `stepId` is the reviewed step's plus '#review', and its `metadata` says what it reviews and who may answer it. A construct with nothing at all below it is not described, and its ordinal is not reused — a gap in ordinals is deliberate, so emitted ordinals must not be assumed dense.

target.description: What the node names: an activity, task, child workflow, tool, or agent. An EVENT_WAIT that waits on alternatives lists them separated by '|'. Absent for control-flow nodes.

label.description: Display text, capped at 120 characters: a branch condition, a looped expression, or an agent's configured model reference. Never part of the identity.

parent.description: The `stepId` of the enclosing control-flow node, for a nested step. Absent at the top level.

branch.description: Which arm of the parent this node belongs to: 'then', 'else', 'body', 'do', 'onFail', or a match clause's patterns.

source.description: For an agent's TOOL node, what backs it.

mode.description: For an EXIT node, which statement ends the flow there.

line.description: One-based source line of the step. Display only — moving code changes it, which is why the identity is an ordinal instead.

column.description: One-based source column of the step.

metadata.description: Extra facts about the node, by kind. For a REVIEW: `reviewedStepId` (the step this review belongs to), `trigger` (ON_FAILURE or PRE_RUN), and whichever of `userRoles`, `title` and `description` the declaration stated literally — a value computed at run time cannot be drawn, and its absence is not a claim that none applies.

edges.description: Directed edges by `stepId`. A workflow's edges follow control flow: sequential between siblings, into each arm of a BRANCH/LOOP/TRY, and from a loop body back to its LOOP node. An agent's edges point inbound from events and tasks to the agent, and outbound from the agent to its model and tools.

when.description: What makes this the edge taken: a branch arm ('then', 'else', a match clause's patterns), loop entry ('body') or re-entry ('repeat'), a do/on-fail arm ('do', 'onFail'), or an agent edge's direction ('in', 'out').
